title: My Chromebook won't turn on
summary: Nothing happens when you press the power button, or the screen stays black.

steps.title: Safety check first
instructions: Look at your Chromebook. Do NOT touch it if it feels very hot.
Check if the bottom is bulging or the case is being pushed apart.
Check for smoke or a burning smell.
steps.question: Do you notice any of these: bulging, very hot, smoke, or a burning smell?

steps.title: Check for damage
instructions: Look closely at your Chromebook.
Check for a cracked screen, liquid spills, missing keys, or a broken hinge.
steps.question: Do you see any damage?

steps.title: Open the lid and press power
instructions: Open the lid all the way. Some Chromebooks turn on when you open the lid.
Press the power button once.
Wait 10 seconds.
steps.question: Did it turn on and show the sign-in screen or your desktop?

steps.title: Turn up the screen brightness
instructions: The screen may be on but turned all the way down.
Find the Brightness up key on the top row of keys. It looks like a large sun.
Press it 5 to 10 times.
steps.question: Can you see the screen now?

steps.title: Check the charger
instructions: Look at the whole charger cable and both plugs.
Look for cuts, frayed wires, bent plugs, or missing pieces.
steps.question: Do you see any damage on the charger?

steps.title: Charge for 30 minutes
instructions: Push the charger plug firmly into the Chromebook.
Push the other end firmly into a wall outlet. If one outlet doesn't seem to work, try a different one.
Leave it plugged in for 30 minutes.
Press the power button.
steps.question: Did it turn on?

steps.title: Do a hardware reset
instructions: Keep the charger plugged in.
Press and hold the Refresh key (the circle arrow on the top row of keys).
While holding Refresh, tap the power button once.
When the Chromebook starts, let go of Refresh.
steps.warning: A hardware reset is NOT a Powerwash. Your account stays on the Chromebook, but files saved only in your Downloads folder might be deleted. Files in Google Drive are safe.
steps.question: Did it turn on?
